title: A pane program declares what it can show, and agents show through that
body:
Agents can show things only in a pane named `code`. The MCP tools `code.show`, `code.mark` and `code.clear` in `src/server/mcp.rs` forward verbs to whatever occupies that pane, and `decade-channel`'s `code` module defines their payloads (`Show { path, line }`, `Mark { path, lines }`). Jack wants a generic "show something", where the program in a pane decides what it can show and highlight.

## Proposal

- At hello, a program declares the kinds it can show. Each kind has a name, says whether it can highlight, and names what its targets are. decade-code would declare `file`, with paths as targets and line ranges as highlights. A browser pane might declare `url`, and an image viewer `image` with no highlight.
- The MCP tools become `show(kind, target, at?)`, `highlight(kind, target, ranges)` and `clear(kind)`. decade routes each call to the pane whose program declared that kind, or to a pane named in the call when several did. decade passes `at` and `ranges` through unread, and each kind gives them their meaning.
- `panes` lists each pane's declared kinds, so an agent can find out what it can show.

## Cost

`decade-channel`'s `code` module gives way to the generic declaration, and `decade-code` in decade-apps updates to match. `decade-channel` is unreleased, so its version stays. `docs/protocol.md` changes with the hello payload.
close_reason: Landed in da499ce, with decade-code updated in decade-apps 19e5b1c. coax still uses the removed code module and is left to its own session.
